messages:
jamie: Hey folks — our customers are seeing 429s in prod starting ~2025-07-12T11:05:00Z. No deploys on our side. Short spikes, not sustained. Any quick ideas?

maya: Sorry about that — can you paste a sample error / headers + whether you have client retries?

jamie: Sample response from our client: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
Headers:
```
x-rate-limit-rpm: 600
x-rate-limit-tpm: 12000
retry-after: 30
x-request-id: rwd-9a8b7c
```
We have a cron that runs every minute and a webhook fanout that runs on schedule too. Both use the same API key. We do exponential backoff but the bursts are tight (many short concurrent requests).

natalie: Looking in Redwood Console for tenant T-42 — I see several 10s spikes where aggregated RPM across regions hit ~700 for ~40s. Our per-token RPM window aggregated those and returned 429s. The TPM stayed below limit but the short RPM pulses tripped the protection.

alex: Eng-oncall here. Hypothesis: token reuse across two independent producers caused interleaving pulses that exceed the per-minute rate cap. Short-term mitigations: 1) add client-side jitter to cron + webhook, 2) smooth fanout (batch or stagger), 3) temporary quota bump for that tenant, 4) better retry backoff (linear then exponential).

maya: Jamie, want us to apply a temporary RPM bump to 800 while you deploy smoothing? Also can you confirm whether requests are evenly distributed across routes or concentrated on one endpoint?

jamie: Please do the bump, thanks. Requests are mostly to `/v1/generate` with a handful to `/v1/embeddings`. I'll roll a jittered cron now.

deploy-bot: Applied quota update for tenant T-42: RPM=800 TPM=15000 — change id INC-12345 — will auto-revert in 6h unless extended.

natalie: Post-bump metrics: the short-term 429 rate dropped from ~12% to <1% in the last 10m. CPU/gpu utilization fine. Recommend client smoothing + remove token sharing if possible.

alex: Follow-ups: (1) Support -> send recommended client changes (sample backoff pseudocode + jitter), (2) Product -> review per-tenant vs per-route aggregation for RPM windows, (3) Eng -> consider adaptive burst allowance for short pulses. I'll open ENG-4567 for tracking.

maya: Jamie — feel free to reopen if you see more 429s after your client change. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
